doc.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Starting guitar: gospel, Isaac Hayes band, Wes Montgomery, Gary
summary: He began at 13-14 with a friend's guitar and his grandfather's church playing, joined an R&B band, found jazz through Wes Montgomery records and learned from Billy Foster in Gary.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You know I wanted to ask you, how did you get started playing the guitar? Who were you listening to at that time or who influenced you or what made you want to be a musician?
Well you know when I first started playing the guitar I was just 14 or 13, and a friend of mine who had a guitar laying around his house all the time, we used to just go around and

play around with the chords or something like that. But my grandfather was a guitar player in the church. So we played in all of the Gospel churches around the South. And I really never thought about playing the guitar, it was just something to do. When I got to be about 13-1/2, I started listening to records, to blues records and Gospel records, and I was playing with Gospel groups. So the Gospel groups, even though it was one group, they were playing in a different church every Sunday. And so by doing that I got drenched with the Gospel stuff too. But the Gospel and the blues is so close that it just adds more to it to me. And after that I was playing in an R&B band, by the time I got to be 14 I was playing in an R&B band which was playing with Isaac Hayes. So that was my first professional gig. And after that, while I was with that band, the bass player brought a record of Wes Montgomery — “Tequila” — and from then on I was listening and I said well what is this, I never heard this, and this is jazz? There was no place around Memphis at that time for me to hear jazz. So I got it strictly through records. So I got that record, and then everybody that was on that record I went and got their records. And then everybody that was on those records, I went and got those records, so it exploded. And after that I started really listening to a lot of jazz, and wanted to play just jazz. And then my family moved back north to Chicago, and it was sort of like Gary, Indiana, was like 35 miles away from Chicago. So I grew up there the rest of the time, and went to high school in Gary. But in the meantime I met another guy who was a jazz piano player in Gary, by the name of Billy Foster. And so he lived right around the corner from me so that was like right home from school, into my room, practice, and run over to Billy’s house, because he had all the records. He had Ahmad Jamal, Miles, he had everybody. So through him I had a chance to learn about other artists that I didn’t know anything about. And I just got entrenched in jazz. And by that time I started playing out around, and I played with him. He had a group for about three years and we just played around Gary and the Chicago area. And then after that I had my own little trio, which I would do all kinds of contemporary music, because at that time you had to play the blues and contemporary music, and everything else to work.
